issue: Auto-ref sequence extracted with .replace('INS-','') instead of regex. When inspectionRef is empty string or malformed, parseInt('',10) returns NaN, so the next ref becomes 'INS-NaN'. Concurrent inserts or any malformed existing record will corrupt all future inspectionRefs permanently.
fix: Replace `parseInt(last.inspectionRef.replace('INS-', ''), 10) + 1` with `const m = last?.inspectionRef?.match(/^INS-(\d+)$/); const seq = m ? parseInt(m[1], 10) + 1 : 1`
standards: CLAUDE.md: Auto-ref sequence generation — NaN protection (May 2026)

issue: loadDemoData() and clearDemoData() actions still declared in AdminService (lines 184, 187). CLAUDE.md explicitly states demo mode was removed (2026-05-12). The actions remain live endpoints accessible to admin/manage roles, backed by demo-data.js (65 KB file still present). This creates a privileged data-manipulation endpoint that should not exist in production.
fix: Remove lines 183-188 from admin-service.cds (the two action declarations). Remove require('./demo-data') from admin-service.js line 5. Remove this.on('loadDemoData') and this.on('clearDemoData') handlers from admin-service.js lines 1850-1860. Delete srv/demo-data.js.

issue: Duplicate srv.after(['CREATE','UPDATE'], 'BridgeLoadRatings') registration — one at line 34 (audit log) and another at line 73 (expiry alert). CAP chains both handlers but the second after handler (expiry alert) silently fires even when data.bridge_ID or data.validTo is null and returns early without error. This is a duplicate registration pattern that is fragile: if either handler throws, the other may or may not run depending on CAP version. More critically, the expiry-alert handler at line 73 runs after the audit handler at line 34 — the audit data passed to logAudit may be stale because the INSERT inside the expiry handler runs concurrently.
fix: Merge both after handlers into a single srv.after(['CREATE','UPDATE'], 'BridgeLoadRatings', async (data, req) => { ... }) that calls logAudit first, then checks validTo for expiry alert.

issue: getNetworkRiskSummary action uses SELECT.from('bridge.management.BridgeRiskAssessments') with no .columns() — fetches all columns including LargeString fields. On a 5,000+ row dataset this will load all text fields into Node.js memory unnecessarily. Similarly getHighRiskBridges at line 68 fetches all columns when only 7 are used.
fix: Add .columns('riskType', 'residualRiskLevel') to the getNetworkRiskSummary query and .columns('bridge_ID','riskType','residualRiskScore','residualRiskLevel','treatmentDeadline','assessor') to getHighRiskBridges query.

issue: getAlertSummary uses SELECT.from('bridge.management.AlertsAndNotifications').where({status:'Open'}) with no .columns(). Fetches all columns including alertDescription (LargeString). On a large alert table this loads all descriptions into memory for a summary count that only needs status, severity, triggeredDate, entityType.
fix: Add .columns('ID','severity','triggeredDate','entityType','status') to the query.

issue: Dashboard handler queries nhvr.Bridge (legacy empty table) instead of bridge.management.Bridges for KPI calculations. nhvr.Bridge uses field names 'isDeleted', 'isActive' that differ from bridge.management.Bridges ('isActive', 'status'). In normal BMS operation, nhvr.Bridge is empty so all KPI endpoints return zeroes. This is confirmed by CLAUDE.md which states nhvr.Bridge is 'a legacy separate table — it is empty in normal operation'.
fix: Replace all SELECT.from('nhvr.Bridge') in dashboard.js with SELECT.from('bridge.management.Bridges') and update field references: 'isDeleted' → 'isActive = false', 'isActive' → 'isActive = true'. Similarly replace nhvr.Restriction with bridge.management.Restrictions.

issue: All async handlers in inspections.js (before CREATE/UPDATE, after CREATE/UPDATE, on deactivate, on reactivate) have no try/catch. An unhandled DB error will propagate as an unhandled promise rejection, crashing the CAP process in Node.js 15+. 13 of 19 handler files have the same issue.
fix: Wrap the async body of each handler in try/catch and call req.error(500, e.message) in the catch block. Files affected: admin.js, alerts.js, capacities.js, conditions.js, dashboard.js, defects.js, elements.js, inspections.js, load-ratings-new.js, load-ratings.js, maintenance.js, nhvr-compliance.js, permits.js, risk-assessments.js.

issue: bridges.js queries nhvr.Bridge (lines 59, 166, 218, 229, 238, 246) with SELECT.one without .columns() on several of these. nhvr.Bridge is a legacy entity that is separate from bridge.management.Bridges — optimistic lock check at line 59 operates on nhvr.Bridge version field, not on bridge.management.Bridges. This means optimistic-lock protection is applied to the wrong entity for the main Bridges CRUD path through AdminService.
fix: Confirm whether BridgeManagementService.Bridges projects nhvr.Bridge or bridge.management.Bridges. If it projects nhvr.Bridge, the version lock is correct. If bridge.management.Bridges, update all SELECT.one.from('nhvr.Bridge') queries to bridge.management.Bridges.

issue: BridgeManagement-srv module has health-check-type: none (line 22) and no memory: property. Without a memory setting, Cloud Foundry assigns the default 1 GB. Without a health check, CF cannot detect a degraded process that is still running but failing requests. The /health endpoint exists (srv/server.js:1154) but is not wired into the MTA health check configuration.
fix: Add `memory: 512M` and `disk-quota: 1024M` under BridgeManagement-srv parameters. Change health-check-type to `http` and add `health-check-http-endpoint: /health` under BridgeManagement-srv parameters.

issue: BridgeManagement-srv module has no NODE_ENV=production property. Without this, Helmet, express, and some CAP features do not apply production-mode hardening. The build step uses --production but the runtime environment variable is not set.
fix: Add `NODE_ENV: production` under BridgeManagement-srv properties section alongside DEFAULT_STATE and APP_VERSION.

issue: APP_VERSION is hardcoded to '1.0.0-nsw-standalone' in mta.yaml properties. This will never automatically reflect the actual package.json version. The /health endpoint returns process.env.npm_package_version || '1.2.0' — mismatching with mta.yaml. When new versions are deployed, operators see '1.0.0-nsw-standalone' in all monitoring dashboards.
fix: Remove the hardcoded APP_VERSION property. Instead read it at runtime from process.env.npm_package_version in srv/server.js (already done there). Or inject it via `APP_VERSION: ${version}` MTA placeholder if needed.

issue: BridgeDocuments entity stores binary file content as LargeBinary in HANA HDI (db/schema/documents.cds line 20). Binary BLOBs in HANA HDI column store are expensive — each row stores the full binary content in the column store page, causing column store spill for files larger than a few KB. No SAP Object Store resource is declared in mta.yaml for off-loading binary storage.
fix: Add a BridgeManagement-objectstore resource (type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service, service: objectstore, plan: s3-standard) to mta.yaml and require it from BridgeManagement-srv. Modify the attachment upload handler in server.js to write content to Object Store and store only the Object Store URL in BridgeDocuments.content (change to String(500)).

issue: getNetworkRiskSummary loads ALL BridgeRiskAssessments rows with no active=true filter and no pagination. At network scale (5,000 bridges × multiple risk assessments = potentially 50,000+ rows) this is an unbounded full-table scan loading all rows into Node.js memory for an in-process aggregation that could be done in SQL with GROUP BY.
fix: Rewrite using `SELECT.from('bridge.management.BridgeRiskAssessments').columns('riskType', 'residualRiskLevel', 'count(1) as cnt').where({active:true}).groupBy('riskType','residualRiskLevel')` and drop the in-process aggregation loop.

issue: getNetworkKPIs and other dashboard functions query nhvr.Bridge with SELECT * (no .columns()). Since nhvr.Bridge is empty in production, these KPIs always return zero/null values, providing misleading dashboard data to all viewers.
fix: Fix CODE-006 first (switch to bridge.management.Bridges), then add explicit .columns() lists to each query.

issue: getNhvrComplianceRate queries nhvr.Bridge (line 26) and nhvr.Restriction (line 69) without .columns(). Both entities are legacy and nhvr.Bridge is empty in production. Compliance rate always returns 0%.
fix: Switch nhvr.Bridge to bridge.management.Bridges and nhvr.Restriction to bridge.management.Restrictions with appropriate field mappings and explicit .columns().

issue: BridgeScourAssessments, BridgeElements, BridgeCarriageways, BridgeContacts, BridgeMehComponents, AlertsAndNotifications, BridgeInspectionElements, NhvrApprovedVehicleClasses, and BridgeDocuments are exposed in AdminService with no @restrict annotation. Any authenticated user can CREATE, UPDATE, and DELETE these records. Only 8 of 30+ entities in AdminService have explicit @restrict blocks.
fix: Add appropriate @restrict blocks matching the pattern used for BridgeInspections (inspect/manage/admin write; view/inspect/manage/admin read; DELETE: []) to each of these entities.
standards: CLAUDE.md: Custom Express routers need explicit requireScope() middleware

issue: The expiry-alert after handler on BridgeLoadRatings (line 73) checks `data.active` but this field is not reliably present in the after-handler data object — CAP after-handlers receive the OData response payload, not the full DB record. If the OData response omits `active`, the guard `!data?.active` will always be true and skip alert creation for all ratings.
fix: Re-fetch the record from DB inside the after handler: `const record = await db.run(SELECT.one.from('bridge.management.BridgeLoadRatings').columns('ID','bridge_ID','validTo','active','ratingRef','vehicleClass').where({ID: data.ID}))` and use record.active/record.validTo/record.bridge_ID.

issue: Severity/urgency comparison uses >= on integer fields but the BridgeDefects schema does not guarantee these are Integer — if the value comes in as a string ('3') from OData, the comparison `d.severity >= 3` evaluates to true (JS type coercion) but `d.severity >= 4` for the alert check also relies on coercion. Inconsistent type handling could cause incorrect alert suppression on string inputs.
fix: Normalise at the top of the handler: `const severity = Number(d.severity) || 0; const urgency = Number(d.urgency) || 0;` then use these normalised values throughout.

issue: writeConditionHistory (line 36-52) inserts into nhvr.ConditionHistory, a legacy entity in db/schema/core.cds. This entity is not exposed through any AdminService or BridgeManagementService projection, and BridgeInspections (bridge.management) is the canonical inspection record. Writing to nhvr.ConditionHistory creates a shadow record in a table with no UI and no data governance, while the canonical audit trail in bridge.management.ChangeLog may be skipped.
fix: Remove the writeConditionHistory call from bridges.js and rely on the BridgeInspections entity for condition history. If condition change history is needed on the Bridges entity directly, write a ChangeLog entry via writeChangeLogs() instead.

issue: getDefectSummary action handler registered in srv/handlers/defects.js (line 115) but this action is declared in srv/services/defects.cds (line 24) under BridgeManagementService. It is NOT declared in srv/admin-service.cds. Users of AdminService (Fiori Elements Bridge ObjectPage) cannot call getDefectSummary — the action 404s.
fix: Add `function getDefectSummary(bridgeId: Integer) returns { totalDefects: Integer; criticalCount: Integer; highCount: Integer; openCount: Integer; completedCount: Integer }` to the BridgeDefects entity actions in srv/admin-service.cds and add a corresponding handler registration in srv/admin-service.js.

issue: admin-service.js imports activateDemoData and clearDemoData from ./demo-data (line 5) which is a 65 KB file. Even after CODE-002 fix removes the action handlers, the require() will still load the entire demo-data.js module into the process on startup. Until CODE-002 is fixed this is an active production risk; after CODE-002 it becomes dead code.
fix: Remove `const { activateDemoData, clearDemoData } = require('./demo-data')` from admin-service.js line 5 as part of the CODE-002 fix.

issue: getNetworkRiskSummary and getHighRiskBridges are registered on BridgeManagementService (via service.js) but are not declared in any AdminService action list. Fiori Elements tiles that call these actions via AdminService will get 404. The actions are only available through BridgeManagementService routes.
fix: Add corresponding function declarations in the BridgeRiskAssessments entity actions in srv/admin-service.cds and register matching handlers in srv/admin-service.js.

issue: Multiple SELECT.one.from('nhvr.Bridge') in bridges.js (lines 59, 166, 218, 229, 238, 246) do not specify .columns(), causing full-row fetches. nhvr.Bridge has JSON fields (geoJson equivalent) and extended attribute columns that inflate each row significantly.
fix: Add explicit .columns() lists to each SELECT.one.from('nhvr.Bridge') call, fetching only the fields actually used in the handler logic below each query.

issue: mta.yaml does not declare a BTP Connectivity service resource. srv/notification-service.js sends notifications and srv/external-api.js provides an external REST facade. While neither currently makes outbound HTTP calls to on-premise systems, if NHVR or TfNSW integration is added the Connectivity service will be required and the MTA will need to be re-deployed. The recon.json 'missing_resources' field explicitly flags this gap.
fix: Add a BridgeManagement-connectivity resource (type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service, service: connectivity, service-plan: lite) to mta.yaml resources section and add it to BridgeManagement-srv requires if outbound on-premise calls are planned.

issue: admin.js SELECT.one.from('nhvr.RoleConfig') (line 18) fetches without .columns(). nhvr.RoleConfig is in admin.cds with a managed aspect — fetches include all managed fields unnecessarily for an existence check.
fix: Add .columns('ID') for the existence check query.

issue: getNhvrAssessmentHistory and related functions in nhvr-compliance.js use SELECT.from('bridge.management.NhvrRouteAssessments') and SELECT.from('nhvr.Restriction') without .columns(). These queries load full rows including all text fields.
fix: Add explicit .columns() to each SELECT.from call in nhvr-compliance.js, fetching only fields used in the response mapping.

issue: ChangeLog entity defines fieldName as String(111) and objectId as String(111), but bridge.management.Bridges.ID is Integer. Storing integer IDs as String(111) wastes storage and prevents numeric comparison filtering. objectType uses a 40-char string but actual values are up to ~25 chars — acceptable but inconsistent with the 111-char pattern.
fix: Change ChangeLog.objectId to String(255) (to accommodate both UUID and integer keys cleanly), fieldName to String(200) (field paths can be longer in nested objects). No behavior change needed — purely defensive widening.

issue: capacities.js uses SELECT.one.from('bridge.management.BridgeCapacities') without .columns() for the existence check in deactivate/reactivate handlers, loading all 30+ decimal fields unnecessarily.
fix: Add .columns('ID','active','capacityType') for the existence/state check queries.

issue: BridgeManagement-app-deployer module missing `memory` and `disk-quota` parameters. The app deployer runs npm ci and mbt build artifacts — without memory limits it will use CF defaults which can be too low for large frontend builds (16 HTML5 apps).
fix: Add `memory: 256M` and `disk-quota: 1024M` under BridgeManagement-app-deployer parameters.

issue: elements.js SELECT.one.from('bridge.management.BridgeElements') (lines 16, 22, 29) fetches without .columns(). Line 29 uses SELECT.from (not SELECT.one) for the auto-ref sequence query, fetching all columns when only the elementId field is needed.
fix: Add .columns('elementId') to the sequence query at line 29 (equivalent to inspectionRef pattern). Add .columns('ID','active','elementId') to deactivate/reactivate existence checks.

issue: common.js helper fetches nhvr.Bridge and nhvr.Restriction (lines 7, 12, 17, 37) without .columns(). These helpers are called by restrictions.js and bridges.js and load full rows for lookups that only need the ID and a name field.
fix: Add .columns('ID','bridgeId','bridgeName') to nhvr.Bridge lookups and .columns('ID','restrictionRef') to nhvr.Restriction lookups in common.js.

issue: Demo actions loadDemoData/clearDemoData are listed in recon.json events list for AdminService (line 1174). Any BTP role with admin or manage scope can accidentally trigger these actions from an OData client or REST tool, loading or wiping demo data on the production system. No guard prevents production execution.
fix: This is a duplicate of CODE-002 — remove the actions entirely. If demo data functionality is needed for UAT/staging environments only, gate it behind an environment check (process.env.DEMO_ENABLED === 'true') in admin-service.js before the handler logic.
